purpose_today: dev.nebius.com is Nebius's developer/builder marketing hub — a thin top-of-funnel landing layer that routes AI builders into one of three products (AI Cloud, Token Factory, Serverless AI) plus the partner Tavily. It is NOT a docs site and NOT an interactive portal: it is a curated set of marketing + 'how-to' jump pages whose job is to (a) pitch each product in one hero line, (b) hand off to the real docs at docs.nebius.com / docs.tokenfactory.nebius.com, the console (console.nebius.com / tokenfactory.nebius.com), GitHub cookbooks, YouTube playlists, and the Discord community, and (c) capture newsletter signups. Every real surface (full documentation, pricing, console/login, code, video) lives on other Nebius subdomains; dev.nebius.com mostly aggregates and links out to them. Think 'developer relations landing site / link hub', not 'product app'.

notes: Holistic read: dev.nebius.com is the same Gravity-UI + Page-Constructor + Directus + Next.js stack Nebius uses for its main marketing site, scoped to a 'for developers/builders' funnel. Its real job is segmentation and hand-off, not hosting product surfaces. Four entry products: AI Cloud (raw GPU VMs/K8s/Slurm-Soperator/SkyPilot, full-control), Token Factory (OpenAI-compatible inference API for open models + dedicated endpoints + post-training), Serverless AI (containerized Jobs + Endpoints, no infra mgmt), and Tavily (partner web-search API). Token Factory page is the most 'product-doc-like' (dense link directory + integration matrix + Playground). Serverless page shows several 'coming soon' blocks, indicating it is the newest/most-in-progress section. Compared to a richer 'builders' site, dev.nebius.com is deliberately thin: no native model library/catalog, no leaderboard, no on-site community/forum, no events calendar, no project gallery, no developer portal/dashboard, and no on-page interactive code or pricing — every one of those is either absent or delegated to an external subdomain (console, docs, GitHub, Discord, nebius.com/events, nebius.com/prices, nebius.com/blog). If the goal is to PORT/replace this with a fuller builders experience, the gaps to add are: an in-site model library with model cards, a leaderboard/benchmarks surface, an events/community hub, a project/showcase gallery, indexed library search, and possibly on-page pricing + interactive code — while the existing strengths to preserve are the clean product-router IA, the integration matrix, the quickstart (Docs+Video+Examples) triplets, and the community/programs link hub. Stack to match if porting: Next.js + Gravity UI + Page Constructor blocks + Directus CMS (the repo this discovery lives in, nebius-homepage, already appears to use Directus + Gravity pc-*/g-* conventions per the existing product landing pages).
